decisions.name: bootstrap
decisions.conflict: The repository provider e2e scenario has a 30-second server-readiness polling budget. In this Windows NTFS worktree under WSL Ubuntu20, two fresh-server attempts timed out before any daemon log; a separate unchanged production-bootstrap diagnostic then reached genuine pairing readiness successfully in 83162 ms and exited normally. This is distinct from the real Codex cold-start test: that existing 60000ms startup budget passed and must remain unchanged. We must obtain authentic browser-save evidence without changing product code, permanent tests or claiming that the 30-second e2e startup passed.

options.A: Use a planning-only browser acceptance harness with a 120-second production-server staging readiness budget, retain the actual bootstrap, isolated data/profile, real native inference, every save/status/GET/SQLite/model-switch assertion and native 60000ms cold-start budget. Record actual boot latency and state explicitly that this does not prove the original 30-second e2e server startup. Leave repository tests unchanged.
options.B: Move real browser acceptance to the normal Windows Node/Git/native Codex environment in the same task worktree, prepare Windows dependency bindings and an isolated Windows data directory, then rerun the unmodified 30-second server-readiness scenario. Keep WSL workspace testing isolated but incur another platform dependency preparation.
options.C: Keep the 30-second readiness budget unchanged and leave real browser evidence and the affected contracts pending until an allowed faster host/runtime becomes available; report the implementation incomplete without a pass/ready claim.

decisions.name: lock
decisions.conflict: The unchanged Linux production bootstrap uses one fixed system-wide /var/lib/agent-scheduler/daemon.lock, independent of AGSCHED_DATA_DIR and HOME. Fresh scratch servers therefore collide, and a stale record from an earlier owned diagnostic now has a PID reused by an alive unrelated test process; the guard correctly refuses to delete that uncertain lock. No global lock should be removed. We need isolated authentic product sessions without changing code or bypassing the native guard. WSL root supports mount namespaces and tmpfs in the assigned planning directory.

options.A: Launch each unchanged production bootstrap in a private Linux mount namespace. Bind a fresh lock directory under its assigned planning tmpfs data root onto the normal fixed system lock path only inside that namespace. Keep real native lock permissions/ownership/guard, full main/container, real CLI/API/SQLite/DOM and isolated profile. Record this host namespace staging clearly. Never remove or modify the host lock.
options.B: Use an isolated planning bootstrap that calls the production startDaemon/createContainer services through their existing DI interfaces with a genuine native lock adapter configured to an explicit private filePath. Real HTTP, SQLite and CLI remain unchanged, but record that the default main composition entry is not used.
options.C: Keep default bootstrap without isolation and leave native browser proof/contracts pending until the global holder state permits startup; report incomplete, do not fabricate success.

decisions.line: adjudicate: pick=A(high 0.92) spec_change=no(0.12) outside_stack=no(0.30) needs_owner=no(0.07) reversible=yes(0.71) adopt=take(A)
